title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance, ADRs
author: Evelyn Park
body:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's cross-cutting architecture and standards for service APIs, code quality, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, performance testing, and key architectural decisions (ADRs). It is the canonical reference for engineers and technical product managers when designing or changing services that participate in inference workflows (hosted API, Dedicated, Private).

Goals
- Provide consistent, reviewable standards to reduce integration errors and operational toil.
- Optimize for predictable performance, maintainability, and secure defaults.
- Make rollout, rollback, and fallbacks explicit for model-serving paths.

Scope
Applies to: Redwood hosted API, Dedicated runtime components (route-service, inference-runtime, cache-service), private control plane adapters, SDKs and publicly exposed REST endpoints.

1) API Standards\nPurpose: Ensure APIs are discoverable, versioned, and reliable for SDKs and customers.\n
- Contract & Schema
  - Use OpenAPI 3.1 for externally facing REST APIs; keep spec in api-specs/ repo.
  - Each API must include request/response schemas, examples, and semantic version in x-api-version header.
  - Support both JSON and application/json-seq for streaming endpoints where applicable.

- Versioning and Compatibility
  - Semantic versioning for public endpoints: major.minor.patch. Major version changes require ADR and migration plan.
  - Backward-compatible additions (new optional fields) allowed within minor versions.
  - Deprecation: announce in release notes and provide at least 90 days before disabling.

- Idempotency & Retries
  - POST operations that create resources must support an Idempotency-Key header.
  - For transient failures, clients should retry with exponential backoff (base 200ms, max 5s, max 5 attempts).

- Pagination & Filtering
  - Cursor-based pagination preferred; include next_cursor and limit.
  - Use standard filter query params: ?created_after=, ?model=, ?status=.

- Errors & Observability
  - Use standard error envelope: { code, message, details[] } and map to HTTP status codes.
  - Include X-Request-ID in responses; services must log it and propagate for tracing.
  - Rate limit headers: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset.

- Security
  - All public APIs require bearer token authentication (OAuth2 tokens or API keys).
  - TLS 1.2+ enforced on ingress; HSTS for web endpoints.

2) Coding Standards
- Language & Frameworks
  - Follow idiomatic patterns for primary languages (Go for core infra, Python for evals and tooling, TypeScript for console).

- Linting & Formatting
  - Enforce linters in CI: golangci-lint for Go, ruff/black for Python, eslint/prettier for TS.
  - PRs must pass static analysis and unit tests before merge.

- API Clients and DTOs
  - Keep data transfer objects (DTOs) small and explicit. Avoid large, untyped maps across service boundaries.
  - Use generated clients from OpenAPI where possible; hand-written clients require ADR.

- Testing
  - Unit test coverage: target 60%+ for new services.
  - Integration tests for API contracts (CI job that validates against live or staging spec).
  - Contract tests for model-serving: include golden prompt set checks (see prompt-sets-and-benchmarks).

- Security Practices
  - Secrets must be stored in KMS-backed secret store. No secrets in repo.
  - Use principle of least privilege for service accounts.

3) Infrastructure Standards
- Accounts & Networking
  - Organize cloud accounts by environment: prod, staging, dev. Infrastructure-as-code (IaC) lives in terraform/ with per-environment workspaces.
  - Network segmentation: inference-runtime and GPU pools must be in private subnets; control plane endpoints in restricted subnets.

- Terraform & IaC
  - All infra changes via PR and tfplan; state stored in remote backend with locking.
  - Modules: use canonical shared modules (vpc, iam, k8s-cluster, autoscaling).

- CI/CD
  - Build artifacts must be immutable and signed.
  - Rollout strategy defaults to canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated metrics checks.

- Capacity & Autoscaling
  - GPU fleet autoscaling policies defined in gpu-fleet-and-capacity; minimum reserved nodes for Dedicated deployments.

4) Model-Serving Standards
- Model Onboarding
  - Each model must have a model manifest: name, id, architecture, tokenizer spec, quantization profile, expected memory and throughput. Store manifest in model-catalog repo.
  - Validation suite: stateless smoke tests, correctness on golden prompts, perf baseline on canonical inputs.

- Quantization & Profiles
  - Supported quantization presets: fp16 (default for high-accuracy), 8-bit (Q4_K_M, Q4_K_S) for cost-sensitive workloads.
  - Recommendation engine (Redwood Optimize) should provide a default quantization suggestion per workload.

- Runtime Behavior
  - KV cache TTL: default 300s for short-lived sessions; configurable per-customer.
  - Batching: inference-runtime should support dynamic batching with max batch size per model manifest.
  - Prefix caching: enable automatic prefix caching for chat sessions where applicable.

- Fallbacks & Compatibility
  - Define compatible model variants for each public model (e.g., model-v1, model-v1-quant8, model-v1-fp16).
  - Smart routing policy: route by latency SLO, region, and cost tier; fall back to lower-cost variant when capacity constrained.

- Rollouts & Quality Guards
  - Canary model rollouts should run on 1–3% traffic with automated quality checks (perplexity delta, eval prompts score, token-level output checks).
  - Automatic rollback if regression > threshold (see regression-triage).

5) Observability Standards
- SLOs & SLIs
  - Core SLOs: availability (99.9% per-month for hosted API control plane), P99 latency for text generation endpoints (<= 2s for short completion models, developer to set per-model).
  - Track SLIs: request_success_rate, p50_latency, p95_latency, p99_latency, error_rate, autoscale_events.

- Logging & Tracing
  - Structured JSON logs: include timestamp, service, level, request_id, model_id, route_id, latency_ms.
  - Distributed tracing: use W3C Trace Context; propagate traceparent and tracestate.

- Metrics & Dashboards
  - Expose Prometheus metrics with stable metric names. Create per-route dashboards in Grafana (cost, latency, error rate, tokens/sec).
  - Alerts: page on SLO burn rate > 4x baseline or sustained error_rate > 1% for 5 minutes.

- Retention & Privacy
  - Logs: 90 days searchable; traces: 30 days. Sensitive customer prompt data must be redacted unless customer opts into longer retention.

6) Performance Standards & Benchmarking
- Latency Targets
  - Define per-model latency SLOs in model manifest. Default p95 targets: 200ms for embeddings, 500ms for small completion models (<1k tokens), 2000ms for larger models.

- Load & Stress Testing
  - Benchmarking harness (benchmarking-and-perf-suite) must be used for major model and infra changes. Include steady-state throughput tests, tail-latency profiling, and cold-start measurements.

- Cost/Performance Tradeoffs
  - Use Redwood Optimize to maintain a performance/cost score per route; include recommendation thresholds for switching quantization or batch size.

7) Decision Records (ADRs)
- ADR-001: Adopt OpenAPI 3.1 for external REST surfaces (2025-02-15). Rationale: tooling ecosystem and client generation.
- ADR-002: gRPC internally for high-throughput binary IPC between route-service and inference-runtime (2025-06-10). Rationale: lower latency and stronger typing.
- ADR-003: Standardize model manifests and quantization profiles (2026-01-12). Rationale: consistent perf profiling and automated routing.
- ADR-004: Canary-first rollouts for model and infra changes with automated metric checks (2026-03-01).

For each ADR include: status, date, author, decision, consequences, and migration plan. ADR canonical repo: architecture/adrs/.

8) Release, Rollout, and Rollback Procedure
1. Create PR with code + spec changes and update OpenAPI and model-manifest where applicable.
2. CI runs unit + contract tests and a smoke deployment to staging.
3. Rollout to canary (5% traffic) with automated evaluation tasks.
4. Monitor SLOs and run regression checks on golden prompt sets.
5. Promote incrementally to 25% and then 100% if checks pass.
6. If regression detected, execute rollback playbook (oncall + owner team) and open incident.

9) Roles & Ownership
- API standards owner: eng-developer-experience.
- Model-serving owner: eng-serving-runtime.
- Infra owner: eng-infra.
- Observability owner: eng-platform.
- Oncall rotations and SLO ownership documented in eng-sre/runbooks.

10) Templates & Examples
- OpenAPI snippet (example endpoint):

  paths:
    /v1/generate:
      post:
        summary: Generate text from a prompt
        x-api-version: 1.0.0
        requestBody:
          required: true
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/GenerateRequest'

- Model manifest snippet:
  name: "redwood-llm-small"
  id: "redwood-llm-small-v1"
  architecture: "transformer-decoder"
  quant_profiles: ["fp16", "q4_k_s"]
  p95_latency_target_ms: "500"

11) Enforcement & Exceptions
- Standards are enforced via CI checks, code review, and architecture review board for major changes.
- Exceptions require an ADR or a signed exception ticket in policies-and-process/change-management and must list compensating controls.

Related Pages
- architecture-standards-principles-and-adrs-2026-03-04 (canonical principles and ADR index)
- runtime-architecture-2026-05-12 (serving runtime architecture overview)
- regression-triage (quality guardrails and rollback thresholds)

Appendix: Quick checklist for PR reviewers
- Is OpenAPI spec updated (if API change)?
- Are new fields backward-compatible or is there a migration plan?
- Do changes include metrics, logs, and trace propagation?
- Are model manifests updated and performance baselines provided?
- Does CI include contract and integration checks?

Contact & Feedback
For questions or proposals to change these standards, open a PR against this document in the architecture repo and ping the reviewers list.
summary: Consolidated architecture and standards covering API, coding, infra, model-serving, observability, performance, and ADRs. Provides prescriptive rules, ownership, and rollout procedures.
